name: Chile 2015–16 (Sampaoli Copa América 2015 to Pizzi Centenario 2016)
scopeNote: Chile national team from the Copa América 2015 opener (11 June 2015, 2-0 v Ecuador) to the Copa América Centenario final (26 June 2016, v Argentina, penalties). Two managers: Jorge Sampaoli (to his January 2016 resignation; 2018 WC qualifiers Oct-Nov 2015 fall in his spell) and Juan Antonio Pizzi (from late January 2016; first matches 2018 WCQ March 2016). Style label used by sources: Bielsa-derived high pressing / juego de posición ('Posesión 74'), 3-4-1-2 / 4-1-2-1-2 (2-1-4-1-2) with fluid back three; under Pizzi 4-2-3-1 / 4-3-3 / 3-4-1-2, less radical. Spielverlagerung preview and Bolivia analysis are 2015 only. Exact dates of Sampaoli resignation (11 Jan 2016) and Pizzi's start (29 Jan 2016 announcement) are from memory/press; the Pizzi announcement is dated 30 Jan in the source. Nothing from 2014 World Cup or 2017 Confederations Cup is used as evidence. No set-piece source found.
openQuestions: Exact date of Sampaoli's departure (announced resignation 11 Jan 2016, from memory) and Pizzi's first day (announced 29/30 Jan 2016, took charge 'next week') not verified from mined pages.
Spielverlagerung preview says back five man-marking of dropping players; no explicit zonal/man statement for the full team; Bolivia analysis only notes Bolivia's man-marking, not Chile's.
No source on Chile's set-pieces; 2018 WCQ matches Oct-Nov 2015 (Sampaoli) not covered by any tactical page.
Pizzi's press-conference date (5 June 2016) inferred from article of 6 June; eventDate kept as 2016-06.
FourFourTwo preview calls Sampaoli's system '3-4-3' while Spielverlagerung gives 3-4-1-2 / 4-1-2-1-2; El Gráfico: 3-5-2 and 4-3-3 with a back three in possession progression.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Sampaoli has used a 3-4-1-2 regularly with great success over the last couple of years however has employed a formation with two centre backs at times. My best guess is that they will use a 4-1-2-1-2 formation against inferior opposition to gain control higher up the field however they will use a 3-4-1-2 against the better teams

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile build up from very deep, drawing out the opposition. The centre-backs spread to the corners of the 18-yard area to make them more difficult to press as play is stretched over a wider area.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile are also extremely fortunate that they have a goalkeeper who is very comfortable on the ball under pressure and is arguably the best ‘keeper at passing in the world. Bravo has no problem playing 50-yard passes to feet and will often come out as far as about 35 yards to help switch play.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile’s wingbacks play on the last line in the final third, hugging the touchline. This makes the opposition fullback either go to mark them, thus leaving the halfspace open, or leave them in space

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile also consistently exercise elements of Juego de Posicion, with their own style often being referred to as ‘Posesion (Spanish) 74’.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile do most of their defending in the opposition’s half and their aggressive pressing and counterpressing is what has made them such a footballing cult. They are always looking to win the ball instead of just dropping off

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile set up a high press with the man on the ball almost always being pressed, usually by the ever-energetic Sanchez. Their back five allows them to man-mark men dropping to receive the ball from their defenders without leaving too much space in behind.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Chile play a very compact pressing game and a high line to accompany it. However, when this press is breached for whatever reason this leaves them highly vulnerable.

sources.title: Copa America Preview: Chile (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Their positioning in possession allows them to be effective at counterpressing as shown below. Chile have made a wall of protection with Aranguiz, Vidal, and Millar.

sources.title: Pizzi making his presence felt (FIFA)
sources.evidence: Pizzi had no qualms in switching to a 4-3-3 line-up for the second group match against Bolivia, shelving the 4-2-3-1 he had begun the tournament with, though he would fall back on it for the final, part of his plan to cut the supply lines to Lionel Messi. He even tried out a more balanced 3-4-1-2 formation

sources.title: Pizzi making his presence felt (FIFA)

sources.title: Pizzi making his presence felt (FIFA)

sources.title: Pizzi making his presence felt (FIFA)

sources.title: Pizzi making his presence felt (FIFA)
